mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in FEDFUNDS above 2.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in UNRATE below 6.0% for two consecutive months indicates weakening labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, which in turn drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained quarterly decline in GDPC1 for two consecutive quarters signals a contraction in aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO of more than 1.0% signals a sharp contraction in industrial production, which reduces corporate revenue and profit expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase in HOUST and a decrease in RSAFS signals rising housing demand but falling savings, indicating consumer leverage expansion, which historically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 0% and RSAFS < 0% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> 0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS are cut by at least 0.5% in a single month, signaling an easing cycle, and UNRATE is above 5.5%, the combination historically drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to lower borrowing costs and stable labor demand.
regime_hint: monetary easing with stable labor market
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> 1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS above 0.5% coincident with a decline in UNRATE below 5.0% suggests labor market churning with job creation outpacing unemployment reduction, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to uncertainty and margin compression.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 0.5% and UNRATE monthly change < -0.5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation exists between monthly increases in GDPC1 and positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns, reflecting rapid demand expansion that boosts earnings expectations in the near term.
failure_condition: The correlation between monthly GDPC1 changes and S&P 500 5-day forward returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in out-of-sample tests.
